---
title: "NGS day 1: Quality control"
---

Today we will look at raw sequencing reads and check whether they are good enough to work with. We will use FastQC, MultiQC and fastp on the cluster, run in containers and submitted with SLURM.

### Learning outcomes

After today you can:

- explain how short-read and long-read sequencing work, and choose a platform for a question
- explain why QC of sequencing data is necessary
- interpret a FastQC report and its warnings, for DNA and for RNA data
- run tools in containers and submit them as SLURM jobs
- decide whether reads need trimming, and check the result

### In class discussion

We will talk about these questions in class. Think about them before you come.

1. Your sequencing facility sends a report that says all samples passed. Why check quality yourself?
2. FastQC marks "per base sequence content" red for RNA-seq data. Is that a problem? Would it be for DNA?
3. Why do we link to the data instead of copying it into our own folder?
4. What does a container solve that installing the tool yourself does not?
